cards.front: What is the general functional dependence of kinetic energy T on generalized coordinates q and velocities \dot{q}?
cards.back: T = T(q, \dot{q}), a function of both positions and velocities (unlike potential V which depends only on q).

cards.front: State the standard quadratic form of kinetic energy in generalized coordinates.
cards.back: $$T(q,\dot{q}) = \frac12 \sum_{i,j=1}^n a_{ij}(q)\dot{q}_i\dot{q}_j$$ where the coefficients $a_{ij}(q)$ are symmetric functions of the generalized coordinates only.

cards.front: Express a particle's velocity vector $\mathbf{v}$ in terms of generalized velocities $\dot{q}_k$.
How are the coefficients $a_{ij}(q)$ obtained from Cartesian kinetic energy?
cards.back: $$a_{ij}(q) = \sum_\alpha m_\alpha \frac{\partial\mathbf{r}_\alpha}{\partial q_i} \cdot \frac{\partial\mathbf{r}_\alpha}{\partial q_j}$$ where the sum is over all particles.

cards.front: Prove that T is always a homogeneous quadratic function of the $\dot{q}_i$.
cards.back: Substitute the linear expression for each $\mathbf{v}_\alpha$ into $T=\frac12\sum m_\alpha|\mathbf{v}_\alpha|^2$; the result is quadratic in the $\dot{q}$ with coefficients depending only on q.

cards.front: In polar coordinates, write the explicit quadratic form of T for a single particle of mass m.
What happens to the quadratic form of T when the coordinate transformation is time-dependent?
cards.back: Additional linear and constant terms in $\dot{q}$ appear: $T = \frac12 a_{ij}(q,t)\dot{q}_i\dot{q}_j + b_i(q,t)\dot{q}_i + c(q,t)$.
